newsitem.title: UK: Hanson sets spin-off date for Energy.
newsitem.headline: Hanson sets spin-off date for Energy.

text.p: Anglo-American conglomerate Hanson Plc set the date for the final stage of its ambitious four-way break-up Tuesday with the announcement that its Energy Group division will be spun off Feb. 24.
Energy Group, which is mulling a string of acquisitions in Britain and the United States, said it had started talks with a U.S. power marketing company.

The spin-off, which is subject to shareholder approval, will give shareholders one Energy share for every 10 existing Hanson shares held. Hanson shareholders will be asked to vote on the proposal at an extraordinary general meeting on Feb. 21.
Once Energy is split off as a separate company, to be listed in London and New York, the rump Hanson group will consist of a clutch of building firms.

"We are all very enthusiastic about the future of Energy and new Hanson and are convinced that both will benefit from enhanced focus on operations, profitability and future growth prospects," Chairman Lord Hanson said.
The first two spin-offs of Britain's Imperial Tobacco and U.S.-quoted Millennium Chemicals Inc. took place last October.
Energy, which will be large enough to rank inside Britain's top 100 blue chips and the Fortune 500 in the United States, is the last to be split off.

Its new management team is led by Derek Bonham, executive chairman, with two joint chief executives to run operations at the main businesses -- Peabody mining and Eastern, the British electricity division.

Bonham told a press briefing the group planned to target a number of acquisitions, particularly in the United States, and admitted entering into "exclusive and confidential" talks with a U.S. power marketing company.
